headline: Bloomberg reports that Nscale's flagship data center in Norway is running only 6.4 of a planned 30 megawatts as the AI cloud company prepares to go public.
score_reason: Pool score kept: useful warning about AI capacity delays, but second-hand and Nscale's side is not in the text read.
importance_line: Matters to investors in the planned listing and to customers such as Microsoft and Anthropic who are waiting for capacity; the account comes from Bloomberg as relayed second-hand and Nscale's response is not in the text read.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Startup Fortune, that Nscale's Narvik site in Norway, built with energy group Aker, has been hit by cooling leaks, permitting fights, delays and a fire, and that workers are housed on a floating hotel. Nscale, a UK provider of rented AI computing power, has filed to list in New York at a valuation of roughly $35 billion and lost $1.02 billion on $140.6 million of revenue in the first half of 2026.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked; text read via Startup Fortune, which credits Bloomberg.
